answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy charges each new identity a real resource cost: a mined proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with network growth. Like a sable that must hunt for every meal, a fake farm pays compute for every head it spawns. Long-lived identities accumulate stake and reputation, so attacking the inlet of new accounts yields little; honest nodes, rooted like willow, grow deeper value over time than disposable clones ever can.
